exposure: fetal neck mass characteristics (size, location, type)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 18 patients diagnosed with fetal neck masses via prenatal ultrasonography at Peking Union Medical College Hospital or referred there between January 2018 and November 2023.
finding: The study found that fetal neck masses are rare benign lesions, with 72% of cases having a favorable outcome, and accurate prenatal evaluation of mass characteristics is crucial for prognosis assessment and management.
mod_finding: Sixteen out of 18 fetuses with neck masses were delivered by elective cesarean section, while two were born via induced labor, indicating that delivery mode selection is a crucial aspect of management.
followup_time: The average postnatal follow-up time was 27 months, with the longest follow-up being 6 years.
gest_age: The mean gestational age at which fetal neck masses were first detected was 27 ± 6 weeks (range 17-38 weeks).
